title: Running account balance
statement:
Table transactions(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account TEXT, day INTEGER, amount INTEGER). amount is positive for a deposit and negative for a withdrawal. Several transactions can happen on the same day; within a day they happen in increasing id order. Every account starts at 0.

For every transaction, return the account, the transaction id and the account's balance right after that transaction (the sum of the amounts of every transaction of the same account up to and including this one).

Sort by account, then in the order the transactions happened (day, then id).

Output: columns account, id, balance.
Constraints: up to 10000 transactions, amounts from -1000 to 1000, ids are not in day order. A solution that recomputes each balance from scratch is too slow for the largest tests.

Example
transactions:
  (1, 'cash', 1, 100)
  (2, 'card', 1, 50)
  (3, 'cash', 2, -30)
  (4, 'cash', 1, 20)
  (5, 'card', 3, -80)
Output:
card|2|50
card|5|-30
cash|1|100
cash|4|120
cash|3|90
starter_code:
-- Table: transactions(id INTEGER PRIMARY KEY, account TEXT, day INTEGER, amount INTEGER)
SELECT account, id
FROM transactions
;
